column1: Compared with a neutral macro communiqué, holding at a restrictive 5.25–5.50% while continuing balance-sheet runoff and stressing “inflation risks” signals risk‑management hawkishness despite “solid” growth; in Taylor-rule and Clarida–Galí–Gertler terms, policy remains above neutral given the inflation gap and still‑tight labor conditions. Incorporating the Financial Stability Report, persistent inflation and ongoing monetary tightening are highlighted as key risks, with residual banking‑sector stress from the spring 2023 failures (SVB, Signature, First Republic) and commercial real estate vulnerabilities likely to keep credit conditions tight; these headwinds temper the upbeat “sound and resilient” banking-system language. FSR‑noted mitigants (for example, backstops like the BTFP and supervisory coordination) reduce tail risks but do not remove the drag from tighter credit. Balancing “solid” activity with elevated macro‑financial risks, the tone is modestly positive but more cautious than before. sentiment score = 0.08
